title: Dashboard orchestration checklist and span-sampling notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist for orchestrating dashboard panels, automated annotation of traces, and a lightweight span-sampling policy tuned for inference workloads. Aim: reduce investigation time for operators while keeping trace-volume and query-costs bounded.

Context / motivation:
- We have many dashboards assembled by hand; onboarding teams copy panels and diverge in signal definitions.
- Traces are the most helpful artifact for root cause but expensive at scale; we need deterministic, explainable sampling that ties to dashboard anchors.
- Operators want a compact investigation flow: panel -> trace anchor -> reproducible ticket template.

Quick choreography (operator flow):
1) Alarm triggers (SLO breach / latency spike).
2) Alert payload includes top-3 affected dashboard panels and a sampled trace-id list produced by the sampling-policy service.
3) Operator opens 'investigation canvas' panel which shows session sketch + top KPI slices (tenant, model, route).
4) From canvas, operator can jump to trace with 1-click; trace view shows span annotations mapped to the panel metric (anchor).
5) Create incident ticket pre-filled with structured fields from the trace anchor (kv-cache hit rate, batch size, seq len distribution).

Panel manifest pattern (recommended metadata to store per panel):
- panel_id: unique dashboard panel id
- display_name: short label
- metric_definition: short text (e.g. p95_inference_ms per route filtered by model_id)
- trace_anchor: rule that selects a span or composite span key (see sampling rules)
- suggested_queries: list of saved queries (SQL/PromQL)
- operator_tags: e.g. 'kv-cache', 'cold-start'
- owner: team/handle

Example panel -> trace_anchor mapping:
- panel: "P95 token-generation latency (hosted)"
- trace_anchor: anchor = AND(span.name contains 'generate_tokens', span.attrs.model_family == 'gpt-like', span.duration > p95)
- sampling-weight: 10x when anchor matches in last 5m

Span-sampling policy (lightweight, deterministic):
- base_rate: 0.5% of requests sampled across the cluster (keeps retention cost steady)
- weighted_rules: list of high-interest selectors that increase sampling weight when matched (weights are multiplicative):
  - long-tail latency rule: span.duration > p95 for route + tenant => weight x20
  - model-change rule: request.model_version != traffic.default_model_version => weight x8
  - kv-cache miss pattern: span.attrs.kv_hit == false AND response.length > 256 => weight x12
  - rollout flag true: request.has_feature.flag('new-runtime') => weight x15
- emergency-sampling: when SLO breach is active for a route, override base rate to 2% for that route for 15m
- deterministic sampling seed: sampling uses request hash + time-window to allow re-sampling the same request id for correlation across systems

Trace annotation contract (what we attach to spans used as anchors):
- anchor_id (string) = panel_id or alert_id that referenced the span
- node_role (string) = 'frontend' | 'gateway' | 'router' | 'inference' | 'kv'
- model_hint (string) = model.family + quantization hint e.g. 'llama2-13b-fp16'
- seq_stats (string) = short encoded 'len=512|prompt_tokens=120|gen_tokens=392'
- cost_estimate (string) = e.g. '0.0034 USD'
Note: anchors must be compact textual fields to avoid increasing trace size dramatically.

Metric definition guidelines (to include in panel manifest):
- name: keep short, human-friendly
- canonical_query: single source-of-truth (PromQL/SQL) saved in obs-config repo
- unit: ms | tokens | usd | count | ratio
- aggregation_window: 1m | 5m | 1h (explicit)
- dimension_keys: tenant_id, route, model_version, region
- guardrails: min_samples_per_window (e.g., 50 requests) to avoid noisy percentiles

Dashboard orchestration checklist (practical):
- [ ] Convert panels to manifest format and store in obs-config repo (path: dashboards/manifests/)
- [ ] Add panel metadata fields: owner, suggested_queries, trace_anchor, cost_estimate_hint
- [ ] Implement small migration job to replace copied panels with templated references (use UID mapping)
- [ ] Add checks in deployment pipeline that ensure canonical_query exists in SQL/PromQL registry
- [ ] Add a lightweight UI that surfaces panel manifest fields for operators (owner, anchor, suggested queries)
- [ ] Define retention tiers: critical-panel-traces (30d), standard (7d), archived (3d) and map panels to tier via manifest
- [ ] Add automated smoke probe that exercises each critical panel's canonical_query nightly and records anomalies

Operator quickcards (copy-to-ticket snippets):
- Incident summary: "p95 latency spike on route=<route> model=<model> observed at <time>"
- Suggested first checks: "1) session warmth index 2) kv-cache miss rate 3) recent rollouts on model or runtime"
- Minimal reproduction prompt: include the prompt hash and seq_stats from the trace anchor
- Attach traces: include anchor_ids and trace_ids (max 5 by default)

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- How many distinct weighted rules before sampling config becomes too volatile? (operational complexity vs signal fidelity)
- Should panel manifests be editable by product teams or only observability stewards? (permission model)
- Cost labeling: do we show per-panel token-cost estimates in dollars or a normalized token-cost score?

Implementation notes / short-term plan:
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): author manifest schema + migration job; add manifest linter to CI; implement base sampling daemon with simple weighted rules.
- Phase 2 (2-3 sprints): UI surface for manifests in Console; link alert payloads to canvas prepopulating trace anchors; implement retention-tier mapping.
- Phase 3 (Q2): integrate automated smoke probes and nightly panel checks; add ML-backed anomaly ranking for which sampled traces to surface first.

References / links used while drafting:
- ENG-4321 (dashboard-manifests migration epic)
- PR: obs-infra/pull/212 sampling daemon sketch
- Confluence: Dashboard Framework + operator canvas (see linked_artifacts)

Notes to self (TODO):
- ping Priya to confirm cost_estimate calc (tokens-per-ms vs raw token counts)
- prototype deterministic-sampler that can be replayed from request-id hash
- add a tiny example manifest for the "P95 token generation" panel and commit under dashboards/manifests/examples/

End.
